# task-40b80c75: fill the enclosed interior

## Confirmed recurrence rule
Given a grid with a complete axis-aligned rectangular outline, recolor only its strict interior cells to color 4; preserve the outline and every other cell. Check all four sides to distinguish a complete rectangle from partial line intersections. Do not infer a broader fill operation from incomplete outlines.

## Evidence
- Demo (13x15, background 1, outline 9): rows 2 and 4 have horizontal outline across columns 9–14; row 3 has side cells at columns 9 and 14. The four interior cells at row 3, columns 10–13 change from 1 to 4. All other cells remain unchanged.
- Accepted test (20x10, background 6, outline 7): rows 13 and 17 have horizontal outline columns 5–9; rows 14–16 have sides at columns 5 and 9. The 3x3 interior (rows 14–16, columns 6–8) changes to 4; all other cells are preserved.

## Practical steps
1. Locate complete rectangles drawn with the line color.
2. Verify the horizontal top/bottom and vertical sides align and enclose an interior.
3. Copy the input and recolor strict interior cells to 4.
4. Preserve frame cells and all cells outside the enclosed area. Check dimensions and every modified coordinate before submitting.
5. Treat color choice as instance-specific evidence: confirmed frames here used 9 and 7, and both interiors became 4. Recheck new demonstrations if the recurrence changes.
